Broadcom announced VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1, a secure, AI‑ and Kubernetes‑native private‑cloud platform that enables production AI workloads with mixed‑compute support for AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs, integrated security, and automation for AI deployment.

Broadcom: Google (Google Cloud) is listed among Broadcom’s custom‑silicon customers, indicating that the hyperscale cloud provider has deployed Broadcom AI XPUs for AI model training and inference workloads.

Broadcom leverages its 2023 acquisition of VMware to integrate AI workloads via VMware Cloud Foundation, providing a software stack that combines Broadcom’s networking and custom silicon with GPU accelerators (including NVIDIA) for cloud and enterprise AI deployments.

Broadcom and OpenAI announced a strategic collaboration to co‑develop systems that combine OpenAI’s custom ASIC (code‑named Titan) with Broadcom’s accelerators and Ethernet solutions, targeting multi‑gigawatt AI compute deployments.
Broadcom extended a financing facility of up to $42 billion to Anthropic to fund AI infrastructure, illustrating a direct financial partnership that supports an AI developer’s compute expansion.

Broadcom: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 includes an AI gateway that brokers access to more than 150 open‑weight and third‑party models, providing developers with a curated model marketplace within the private‑cloud AI stack.

AMD has built an ecosystem of partnerships and programs targeting AI developers and cloud platforms, including collaborations with Meta on AI infrastructure, a strategic AI cloud partnership with Oracle, a deep integration with Microsoft Azure, an investment partnership with Anthropic, the acquisition of Europe’s largest private AI lab Silo AI, and joint offerings with cloud‑native providers OneQode, Nscale and Scaleway. The company also runs an AI Developer Program that offers cloud credits, training and community resources to accelerate developer adoption of AMD CPUs, GPUs and the ROCm stack.

Intel Corp: Intel’s data‑center AI portfolio includes Xeon Scalable and Xeon CPU Max processors, the Xeon 6 line, Gaudi AI accelerators (Gaudi 2 and the announced Gaudi 3), Intel Nervana, Movidius vision chips, and programmable FPGAs, all supported by the oneAPI unified programming model and the OpenVINO inference toolkit.

Intel Corp: Major U.S. cloud providers have publicly announced using Intel AI hardware: Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Microsoft Azure cite Intel Xeon processors and AI accelerators in their training and inference services.

Intel Corp: Intel sustains a broad ecosystem of alliances: cloud partnerships with Google, AWS and Microsoft; system‑integrator collaborations with Accenture, Deloitte and Iron Bow; networking integration with Cisco; and developer programs such as oneAPI, OpenVINO and the Intel Developer Zone that enable AI development for cloud providers and AI developers.

Broadcom’s Tomahawk 6 Ethernet switch, announced in Q2 FY 2025, provides 102.4 Tbps of switching capacity and is positioned for AI data‑center networking, delivering higher bandwidth and lower latency for AI model training and inference workloads.

Broadcom: AI networking products, including Ethernet switches and routers, accounted for roughly 40 % of Broadcom’s AI semiconductor revenue in Q2 FY 2025, highlighting a major focus on high‑performance networking for AI workloads.

Broadcom: S&P Global Ratings identifies Broadcom as the second‑largest AI semiconductor provider worldwide, behind NVIDIA, with AI semiconductor revenues representing 57 % of its total semiconductor sales in Q3 2025 (up from 41 % in FY 2024).
Broadcom reported AI‑related semiconductor revenue growth of more than 60 % year‑over‑year in fiscal 2025, contributing to an overall revenue increase of 23 % for the year.

AMD offers the Instinct MI400 series AI accelerators (MI455X for training/inference and MI430X for HPC) built on the CDNA 5 architecture with up to 40 PFLOP FP4 and 20 PFLOP FP8 compute, and plans the MI500 series for 2027 with next‑gen compute, memory and interconnect capabilities (S1). The data‑center portfolio also includes Instinct MI350X GPUs, 6th‑gen EPYC Zen 6 CPUs and Pensando DPUs, which are integrated in the Helios rack‑scale AI system (S2, S7). On the software side AMD provides the open‑source ROCm driver stack, the Vitis AI 3.0 development platform with AI Engine‑ML and Deep Learning Processing Unit for Versal ACAP devices, and framework integrations such as PyTorch, MIGraphX, Ray and Triton (S3).

AMD: IDC’s AI‑accelerator vendor share data for CY2 Q 2025 shows AMD holding 1.8 % of the AI accelerator market, equivalent to about $850 million in revenue (S13). Independent market estimates place AMD’s Instinct GPU line at $7‑8 billion in 2025, representing roughly 5‑7 % of total AI accelerator revenue (S14).

SANTA CLARA, Calif., July 10, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- [AMD](https://www.amd.com "AMD") (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced the signing of a definitive agreement to acquire [Silo AI](https://www.silo.ai "Silo AI"), the largest private AI lab in Europe, in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $665 million. The agreement represents another significant step in the company’s strategy to deliver end-to-end AI solutions based on open standards and in strong partnership with the global AI ecosystem. The Silo AI team consists of world-class AI scientists and engineers with extensive experience developing tailored AI models, platforms and solutions for leading enterprises spanning cloud, embedded and endpoint computing markets.

Silo AI CEO and co-founder Peter Sarlin will continue to lead the Silo AI team as part of the AMD Artificial Intelligence Group, reporting to AMD senior vice president Vamsi Boppana. The acquisition is expected to close in the second half of 2024.

“Across every industry, enterprises are looking for fast and effective ways to develop and deploy AI solutions for their unique business needs,” said Vamsi Boppana, senior vice president of the Artificial Intelligence Group at AMD. “Silo AI’s team of trusted AI experts and proven experience developing leadership AI models and solutions, including state-of-the-art LLMs built on AMD platforms, will further accelerate our AI strategy and advance the build-out and rapid implementation of AI solutions for our global customers.”

Based in Helsinki, Finland, with operations in Europe and North America, Silo AI specializes in end-to-end AI-driven solutions that help customers integrate AI quickly and easily into their products, services and operations. Their work spans diverse markets, with customers including Allianz, Philips, Rolls-Royce and Unilever. Silo AI also creates state-of-the-art open source multilingual LLMs, such as Poro and Viking, on AMD platforms in addition to its SiloGen model platform.

“At Silo AI, our mission from the start has been to build an AI flagship company. Today's announcement is a logical next step in that pursuit as we join forces with AMD to shape the future of AI computing,” said Peter Sarlin, CEO and co-founder of Silo AI. “We have a well-established history of building successful AI products and delivering value to our customers. We look forward to becoming part of AMD to further scale our impact and develop enterprise solutions and AI models that address the most complex challenges with deploying AI at scale today.”

“As a leading European AI company, Silo AI has been a great long-term partner for us in many AI-related projects. We look forward to the enhanced capabilities the combination of AI technologies and innovative compute solutions from AMD will bring,” said Nishant Batra, Chief Strategy and Technology Officer (CSTO), Nokia.

Silo AI marks the latest in a series of acquisitions and corporate investments to support the AMD AI strategy. AMD has invested over $125 million across a dozen AI companies in the last 12 months and also acquired Mipsology and Nod.ai to expand the AMD AI ecosystem, support partners and advance leadership AMD computing platforms.

“Silo AI has been a pioneer in scaling large language model training on LUMI, Europe’s fastest supercomputer powered by over 12,000 AMD Instinct MI250X GPUs,” said Dr. Pekka Manninen, Director of Science and Technology at CSC-IT Center for Science, Finland. “Together with university collaborators, they have trained state-of-the-art open-source models for EU languages, such as the Nordic Poro and Viking models. We have collaborated extensively with the team in optimizing the software layer, allowing for efficient training of AI models on LUMI.”

“One year ago, Combient partnered with Silo AI, a leading AI lab with 300 AI scientists and engineers. Together with Marcus Wallenberg, we initiated Combient in 2015 to accelerate digitalization and AI adoption for 38 of the largest Nordic companies, with a total turnover of €270 billion, such as H&M, IKEA, Saab, KONE and Ericsson,” said Mats Agervi, CEO of Combient. “Today’s acquisition underscores the capabilities of Silo AI, opening up expanded opportunities for increased value creation in Europe and beyond.”

## AMD MI400 Series Comes In MI455X "Training/Inference" & MI430X "HPC" Variants, Instinct MI500 All Set For 2027

During its Financial Analyst Day 2025, AMD highlighted its MI400 and MI500 series AI GPU accelerators as key highlights. These two Instinct families are really important for AMD's AI strategy moving forward, and the company has reaffirmed its yearly launch cadence to strengthen its AI family against NVIDIA, [which is dominating the segment right now](https://wccftech.com/nvidia-has-already-geared-up-to-challenge-big-tech-custom-ai-chip-ambitions/).

[##### **Related Story** AMD Helion Rack Crams 32,768 EPYC Zen 6 Cores Into One CPU-Only Agentic AI Blueprint](https://wccftech.com/amd-helion-rack-crams-32768-epyc-zen-6-cores-into-one-cpu-only-agentic-ai-blueprint/)

Next year, AMD will launch its [Instinct MI400 series AI accelerators](https://wccftech.com/amd-instinct-mi400-accelerator-doubles-compute-40-pflops-432-gb-hbm4-memory-2026-launch/). The new lineup will be based on the CDNA 5 architecture and offers:

* Increased HBM4 Capacity & Bandwidth
* Expanded AI Formats with Higher Throughput
* Standard-Based Rack-Scale Networking (UALoE, UAL, UEC)

The official metrics list the MI400 as a 40 PFLOP (FP4) & 20 PFLOP (FP8) product, which doubles the compute capability of the MI350 series, which is a hot product for AI data centers.

In addition to the compute capability, AMD is also going to leverage HBM4 memory for its Instinct MI400 series. The new chip will offer a 50% memory capacity uplift from 288GB HBM3e to 432GB HBM4. The HBM4 standard will offer a massive 19.6 TB/s bandwidth, more than double that of the 8 TB/s for the MI350 series. The GPU will also feature a 300 GB/s scale-out bandwidth/per GPU, so some big things are coming in the next generation of Instinct.

* 1.5x Memory Capacity vs Competition

* 1.5x Scale-Out Bandwidth vs Competition

For the MI400 series, there will be two products, the first one is the Instinct MI455X, which is aimed at scale AI Training & Inference workloads. The other one is MI430X, which is aimed at HPC & Sovereign AI workloads, featuring hardware-based FP64 capabilities, hybrid compute (CPU+GPU), and the same HBM4 memory as the MI455X.

In 2027, AMD will be introducing its [next-gen Instinct MI500 series AI accelerators](https://wccftech.com/amd-zen-6-epyc-venice-zen-6-cpus-256-cores-2026-epyc-verano-zen-7-instinct-mi500-gpus-2027/). decision_analysis.executive_summary: Broadcom is rapidly scaling its AI accelerator and networking portfolio, showing >60% YoY revenue growth in FY2025 and strong cloud partner adoption. This creates both immediate competitive pressure for NVIDIA in the AI data‑center market and longer‑term considerations versus AMD’s 2027 roadmap. Key gaps include missing performance benchmarks for NVIDIA products and detailed revenue breakdowns for Broadcom. The analysis identifies two high‑impact opportunities, two material risks, and six actionable recommendations to guide NVIDIA’s cloud partnership, product positioning, and strategic planning.
